<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

The NPU precise-test (coverage-based test selection) pipeline needs better run-page
observability and a quieter, faster teardown:

- **Opaque selection results.** The bucketing step only emitted machine-readable
  `GITHUB_OUTPUT` values, so on the run page there was no way to see which tests
  coverage recommended, which suites were skipped vs. ran a subset, and which
  recommended files matched no suite pool.
- **Broken NPU-only coverage view.** The NPU-only report relied on a separate rcfile
  with `[run] source`, but `source` does not filter at report time — the "NPU-only"
  view was identical to the full report, so the per-tree NPU coverage number was
  meaningless.
- **No per-run artifacts.** precise-test outputs (`outputs.tar.gz`,
  `test_case_map.json`) only lived on the shared publish disk under fixed names that
  race with concurrent runs; nothing was attached to the run itself for debugging.
- **Benign log noise masking real failures:**
  - coverage 7.8: multiprocessing workers that receive the teardown SIGTERM after
    their coverage already stopped die on `assert self._collectors`, printing a
    scary multi-process traceback per worker (tests still pass).
  - CANN `tbe` repository-manager queue-client threads flood the log with ~15-line
    `EOFError`/`ConnectionResetError` tracebacks per process during graceful
    teardown — vendor-inherent and benign.
  - The tbe atexit `rm -rf` of the shared `kernel_meta` compile-cache races with
    sibling ranks still writing `kernel_meta_temp_*` dirs, printing one `rm` error
    line per directory.
- **Slow teardown.** The 20s graceful-kill timeout adds dead time to every test
  run; teardown reliably completes well within 5s.

## Modifications

- **`.github/workflows/pr-test-npu.yml`**
  - Pass `--github-summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` to the bucketing step.
  - Fix the NPU-only coverage view: copy the combined data to `.coverage-npu`,
    `touch_file()` every unexecuted `.py` under `sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu`
    (`os.walk`, so the PEP 420 namespace tree with no `__init__.py` counts fully),
    then filter with `--include`, which does apply at report time; same for the
    summary totals line.
  - Upload a `precise-test-outputs` artifact (`outputs.tar.gz` +
    `test_case_map.json`, ~300MB, 14-day retention, `continue-on-error`) before the
    publish step moves the files into the fixed `PUBLISH_DIR`.
- **`scripts/ci/npu/precise-test/bucket_recommended_tests.py`**
  - New `--github-summary` option / `write_github_summary()`: appends a markdown
    section with the precision-mode state, recommended case count, a per-suite
    table (registered / bucketed / action), and collapsible lists of recommended
    cases, files matching no suite pool, and per-suite buckets.
  - Keep raw case-level entries (with `::case` suffix) for the summary; write job
    outputs before the summary so a summary failure can never cost downstream jobs
    their bucket outputs.
- **`scripts/ci/npu/precise-test/run_tests_with_coverage.sh`**
  - Replace the one-line `.pth` with a `sglang_ci_cov_guard.py` guard module
    (inert unless `COVERAGE_PROCESS_START` is set): makes `Collector.stop`
    idempotent, patches `Coverage._on_sigterm` to flush via the stock atexit path
    and then die quietly via `SIG_DFL`, and installs a structural
    `threading.excepthook` that swallows only the known tbe queue-client teardown
    shape — any traceback with foreign frames still prints in full.
  - Filter benign `rm` errors on `kernel_meta` paths from pytest output
    (`grep -vE`; `PIPESTATUS[0]` preserves the pytest exit code).
  - Default graceful timeout 20s → 5s.
- **`scripts/ci/npu/precise-test/precise_test_coverage_plugin.py`**
  - Graceful timeout default 20s → 5s, kept in sync with the shell script.
## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

-    branches: [ main ]

       coverage_mode:
@@ -674,7 +676,8 @@ jobs:
             --recommended scripts/ci/npu/precise-test/recommended_pytest_paths.txt \
             --suites "base-b-test-1-npu-a3,base-b-test-2-npu-a3,base-b-test-4-npu-a3,base-b-test-8-npu-a3,base-b-test-16-npu-a3,base-c-test-acc-2-npu-a3,base-c-test-acc-16-npu-a3,base-c-test-perf-2-npu-a3,base-c-test-perf-16-npu-a3" \
             --precision-mode "${PRECISION_MODE}" \
-            --github-output "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
+            --github-output "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}" \
+            --github-summary "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}"
 
   # ==================== Coverage Assembly & Publish ==================== #
   # Assembles coverage data and publishes the baseline to the shared disk.
@@ -864,25 +867,38 @@ jobs:
             python3 -m coverage html --rcfile=/tmp/report-rc \
             --directory="${REPORT_DIR}"
 
-          # NPU-only view, generated in parallel with the full report:
-          # denominator = the whole hardware_backend/npu tree, files never
-          # imported by the traced processes count as 0% ([run] source
-          # semantics). source has no report-time CLI flag, so it needs a
-          # separate rcfile; putting it in /tmp/report-rc would shrink the
-          # full report's scope too. [paths] is shared so measured files
-          # still resolve to the covstub copy.
-          {
-            echo "[run]"
-            echo "branch = True"
-            echo "source = ${COVSTUB}/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu"
-            echo "[paths]"
-            echo "sglang ="
-            echo "    ${COVSTUB}/sglang/"
-            echo "    */python/sglang/"
-          } > /tmp/report-rc-npu
+          # NPU-only view: [run] source does NOT filter at report time, so
+          # the old source-based rcfile produced a report identical to the
+          # full one. Instead: copy the combined data and touch the
+          # unexecuted npu .py files into the copy (the same 0% mechanism
+          # coverage uses for source, but via os.walk so the PEP 420
+          # namespace tree — no __init__.py — counts fully), then filter
+          # with --include, which does apply at report time.
+          cp /tmp/.coverage-all /tmp/.coverage-npu
+          python3 - "${COVSTUB}" <<'PYEOF'
+          import os
+          import sys
+          from coverage import CoverageData
+
+          npu_root = os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "sglang", "srt", "hardware_backend", "npu")
+          data = CoverageData(basename="/tmp/.coverage-npu")
+          data.read()
+          measured = set(data.measured_files())
+          added = 0
+          for root, _, files in os.walk(npu_root):
+              for f in files:
+                  if f.endswith(".py"):
+                      p = os.path.join(root, f)
+                      if p not in measured:
+                          data.touch_file(p)
+                          added += 1
+          data.write()
+          print(f"NPU view: {len(measured)} measured, touched {added} unexecuted files")
+          PYEOF
           rm -rf "${REPORT_DIR}-npu"
-          COVERAGE_FILE=/tmp/.coverage-all \
-            python3 -m coverage html --rcfile=/tmp/report-rc-npu \
+          COVERAGE_FILE=/tmp/.coverage-npu \
+            python3 -m coverage html --rcfile=/tmp/report-rc \
+            --include='*/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/*' \
             --directory="${REPORT_DIR}-npu"
 
           # Surface the totals directly on the run page.
@@ -895,8 +911,9 @@ jobs:
               COVERAGE_FILE=/tmp/.coverage-all \
                 python3 -m coverage report --rcfile=/tmp/report-rc | tail -n 1
               echo "python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu (full-tree denominator):"
-              COVERAGE_FILE=/tmp/.coverage-all \
-                python3 -m coverage report --rcfile=/tmp/report-rc-npu | tail -n 1
+              COVERAGE_FILE=/tmp/.coverage-npu \
+                python3 -m coverage report --rcfile=/tmp/report-rc \
+                --include='*/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/*' | tail -n 1
               echo '```'
               echo "Full line-by-line report: download the \`coverage-html-report\` artifact and open \`htmlcov/index.html\` (NPU-only view: \`htmlcov-npu/index.html\`)."
             } >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
@@ -923,6 +940,24 @@ jobs:
           RUN_DIR="/root/.cache/tests/precise-test/${{ github.run_id }}-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}"
           tar -czf "${RUN_DIR}/outputs.tar.gz" -C "${RUN_DIR}" outputs
 
+      - name: Upload outputs and test case map
+        # Report upload must never block the baseline publish pipeline.
+        # Must run before the publish step mv's the files to the fixed
+        # PUBLISH_DIR (fixed names there race with concurrent runs).
+        # ~300MB artifact; short retention beats the 90-day default so
+        # storage does not accumulate across runs.
+        continue-on-error: true
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: precise-test-outputs
+          # Two paths -> artifact root becomes RUN_DIR, so the archive
+          # holds outputs.tar.gz and test_case_map.json side by side.
+          path: |
+            /root/.cache/tests/precise-test/${{ github.run_id }}-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}/outputs.tar.gz
+            /root/.cache/tests/precise-test/${{ github.run_id }}-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}/test_case_map.json
+          if-no-files-found: ignore
+          retention-days: 14
+
       - name: Publish outputs and map to shared disk
         shell: bash
         run: |

@@ -20,12 +20,17 @@
 valid shell identifiers. Any failure path yields empty/missing outputs, which
 callers treat as "run the full suite".
 
+When --github-summary points at $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, a markdown section is
+appended with the recommended test cases, counts, per-suite buckets, and the
+files that matched no suite pool (not run by the bucketed a3 suites).

 """
 
 import argparse
@@ -74,6 +79,87 @@ def enumerate_suite_files(suite: str, work_dir: Path) -> list:

+def write_github_summary(
+    summary_file: str,
+    raw_entries: list,
+    recommended: set,
+    all_pool: set,
+    buckets: dict,
+    suite_pool_sizes: dict,
+    precision_mode: bool,
+) -> None:
+    """Append a markdown section with the recommendation results to the
+    GitHub Actions step summary ($GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY)."""
+    unbucketed = sorted(recommended - all_pool)
+    lines = []
+    lines.append("### Recommended tests from coverage")
+    lines.append("")
+    if precision_mode:
+        lines.append(
+            "Precision mode **on** — a3 suites run only the bucketed subset below."
+        )
+    else:
+        lines.append("Precision mode **off** — suites run in full.")
+    lines.append("")
+    lines.append(
+        f"Recommended **{len(raw_entries)}** test cases "
+        f"({len(recommended)} unique files); "
+        f"{len(unbucketed)} match no suite pool."
+    )
+    lines.append("")
+    lines.append("| Suite | Registered files | Bucketed files | Action |")
+    lines.append("|---|---|---|---|")
+    for suite, files in buckets.items():
+        if precision_mode and suite_pool_sizes[suite] and not files:
+            action = "skipped (no recommended test)"
+        elif precision_mode and files:
+            action = "run subset"
+        else:
+            action = "run full suite"
+        lines.append(
+            f"| {suite} | {suite_pool_sizes[suite]} | {len(files)} | {action} |"
+        )
+    if raw_entries:
+        lines.append("")
+        lines.append(
+            f"<details><summary>Recommended test cases ({len(raw_entries)})</summary>"
+        )
+        lines.append("")
+        lines.append("```")
+        lines.extend(raw_entries)
+        lines.append("```")
+        lines.append("</details>")
+    if unbucketed:
+        lines.append("")
+        lines.append(
+            f"<details><summary>Matched no suite pool — not run by a3 suites ({len(unbucketed)})</summary>"
+        )
+        lines.append("")
+        lines.append("```")
+        lines.extend(unbucketed)
+        lines.append("```")
+        lines.append("")
+        lines.append(
+            "Not registered in any of the 9 bucketed a3 suites — they may still "
+            "run elsewhere (e.g. base-a runs its full suite; nightly tests run "
+            "in nightly pipelines)."
+        )
+        lines.append("</details>")
+    if any(buckets.values()):
+        lines.append("")
+        lines.append("<details><summary>Bucketed test files per suite</summary>")
+        lines.append("")
+        for suite, files in buckets.items():
+            lines.append(f"**{suite} ({len(files)})**")
+            lines.append("")
+            lines.extend(f"- {f}" for f in files)
+            lines.append("")
+        lines.append("</details>")
+    with open(summary_file, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
+    print(f"Summary written to: {summary_file}")
+
+
 def main():
     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
         description="Bucket coverage-recommended tests per CI suite."
@@ -102,21 +188,30 @@ def main():

         help="GITHUB_OUTPUT file to write step outputs to (empty = print only)",
